proof:
The endpoint midpoint interval $[-5/4,5/4]$ lies in $B$, so the lifted hull has the listed fibers: a lifted combination over zero uses equal total weights from the two endpoints, and its other component is in $B$. The endpoint slices are exact by extremality of their bases, with no other integer bases.

For the general source-usage test, if a singleton or midpoint belongs to a closed halfspace $H$, at least one of its sources belongs to $H$, because the complement is convex. The output indicator is thus bounded by the sum of the source indicators, counted with multiplicity. Integrating each coupling and adding gives domination by the sum of physical marginals, hence by the original mixed measure. This works for every ambient closed halfspace.

For the outer pair use uniform $dq$ on $[0,1]$ and the increasing quantile $T(q)$ of the density with four successive values $2/7,\ 9/28,\ 67/140,\ 11/28$ on the intervals with consecutive endpoints $-5/4,-3/4,-1/4,1,5/4$. The masses of those intervals are $1/7,9/56,67/112,11/112$, summing to one, so $T$ is continuous piecewise affine with the reciprocal slopes of those densities. Pair $R(q)=q-1/2$ in $D$ with $L(q)=2T(q)-R(q)$ in $A$. Their midpoint is $T(q)$. The right source exhausts $D$ with density one. The left map increases from $-2$ to $2$ with slopes $6,\ 47/9,\ 213/67,\ 45/11$, so its marginal density is at most one on $A$ and it uses mass one.

For the middle pairs use the two maps
$$
(-1/4+5s,\ 11/4-s),\qquad (-3/4+6s,\ 11/4-s),\qquad 0\le s\le1/2,
$$
with parameter measures $(11/14)\,ds$ and $(3/14)\,ds$. Their right marginals together are Lebesgue measure on $[9/4,11/4]$. The left marginals together have density $1/28$ on $[-3/4,-1/4]$ and $27/140$ on $[-1/4,9/4]$ by the map slopes. Their midpoints have densities $11/28$ on $[5/4,9/4]$ and $3/35$ on $[1,9/4]$, respectively, and output mass $1/2$ in total. The unused part of $B$ is used as singleton outputs of densities $1,\ 27/28,\ 113/140$ on $[-5/4,-3/4],[-3/4,-1/4],[-1/4,9/4]$, respectively. It has mass three, since both middle-pair marginals together have mass one. All statements about piecewise densities are almost everywhere, so shared endpoints of pieces cause no duplicate mass.

On the successive five intervals cut out by $-5/4,-3/4,-1/4,1,5/4,9/4$, the sums of the outer, singleton and middle-pair densities are respectively
$$
2/7+1,\quad 9/28+27/28,\quad 67/140+113/140,\quad
11/28+113/140+3/35,\quad 113/140+11/28+3/35.
$$
All equal $9/7$. The output is supported exactly on $J$ with mass $9/2$, and the source-usage test gives raw domination.

With a common convex factor, tensor each parameter measure by volume on $K$, using the same factor coordinate in both sources of a pair. Product fibers remain actual because the endpoint midpoint product lies in the middle product. Every source and output law tensors by this same volume measure, with output mass $(9/2)|K|$ and input mass $9|K|$. The source-usage test still applies to the physical ambient coordinates and gives $\nu(H)\le2\mu(H)$. For any halfspace containing $(0,1/2,g_K)$ its restriction to base zero contains the centroid of $J\times K$, or the whole product. Apply 6769574fc1bd9f8d with full mass for that $(r+1)$-dimensional convex body to get $\nu(H)\ge\gamma_{r+1}$. This gives the claimed normalized bound. The middle interval's original centroid is $3/4$, and the midpoint of the endpoint centroids has interval coordinate zero, so the transport center differs from both.

statement:
For actual interval fibers $A=[-2,2]$, $B=[-5/4,11/4]$, and $D=[-1/2,1/2]$ at integer bases $-1,0,1$, there is a rational piecewise affine singleton and midpoint transport to base zero whose aggregate physical source marginals are dominated by original mixed volume, counting all occurrences. It produces the uniform measure on $J=[-5/4,9/4]$ of density $9/7$ and mass $9/2$. The components use mass one of outer pairs, mass $1/2$ of same-middle-fiber pairs, and mass three of middle singletons. The aggregate source marginal exhausts $B$ and $D$ and uses mass one of $A$.

For any common compact convex factor $K\subset\mathbb R^r$ of positive $r$-volume, including a point with volume one if $r=0$, replace each original interval by its product with $K$. Let $\mu$ be the resulting normalized mixed measure and $\nu$ the uniform probability law on $\{0\}\times J\times K$. Then $\nu(H)\le2\mu(H)$ for every closed ambient halfspace. The original normalized depth at $(0,1/2,g_K)$, where $g_K$ is the factor centroid, is at least $\gamma_{r+1}/2$ with $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$.
title: An exact uniform halfspace transport for unequal three-interval fibers
